learningObjective: Explain the design intent of Ansor's task scheduler for allocating autotuning budget across subgraphs.
stem: The Ansor paper introduces a 'task scheduler' that allocates autotuning budget across the subgraphs of a full model. Which TWO of the following statements correctly describe the task scheduler's design intent, as argued in the paper?

options.text: The task scheduler distributes budget non-uniformly, favouring subgraphs whose expected marginal improvement × contribution to end-to-end latency is largest, because end-to-end wall-clock time is the objective rather than per-task speedup in isolation.
The task scheduler's motivation is that a uniform-budget baseline (equal time per subgraph) wastes effort on already-optimal or low-contribution subgraphs; the scheduler exists to fix this.
The task scheduler is a runtime scheduler that decides which kernel to launch at inference time; it has nothing to do with autotuning search budget.
The task scheduler enforces that every task must receive at least 10% of the tuning budget so that no task is ever under-tuned.

explanation: The Ansor paper's §5 explicitly introduces the task scheduler to redirect tuning budget toward subgraphs whose end-to-end impact is largest (A), and argues against uniform allocation as a baseline (B). C confuses tuning-time scheduling with runtime execution scheduling. D fabricates a floor rule not present in the paper.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: non-uniform allocation driven by marginal impact on end-to-end time.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: the paper motivates the scheduler by the failings of uniform baselines.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: the task scheduler operates during autotuning, not at inference.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: no such fixed floor rule is described.

assumptions: 'Task' means a subgraph carved out for scheduling in Ansor.
nonImplications: Does not imply Ansor's specific speedup numbers generalize across workloads and hardware.
Does not imply the scheduler ignores per-task convergence; plateau detection is part of the marginal-improvement estimate.

sourceRefs.locator: §5 task scheduler design and comparison to uniform baseline
